chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Durust, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Does the person in ihram place his hand on his wife?' He said: 'There is no harm.' I asked: 'And if he dismounts her from the mount and embraces her?' He said: 'There is no harm.' I asked: 'If he intended to dismount her from the mount, and when he embraced her, desire overcame him?' He said: 'There is no obligation upon him, unless he sought that (intentionally).'

key_terms.الْمَحْمِلُ: The mount or saddle (used for riding)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (pilgrimal consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a pilgrim in ihram touching or embracing their spouse?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the boundaries of permissible physical contact for a muhrim, distinguishing between casual intimacy and deliberate pursuit of sexual release. It establishes that incidental ejaculation due to natural desire carries no penalty, whereas intentional seeking of that state incurs liability, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between *khata'* (error) and *'amd* (intent).
